frequency_question: How often do structural institutional frictions (such as inter-agency vetoes, systemic financial stability concerns, and diplomatic pushback) successfully prevent the actual execution of threatened secondary sanctions against major Tier-1 foreign banks?
membership_rule: Includes formal public warnings or deliberate deliberations regarding Tier-1 foreign banks in allied or major adversary jurisdictions for sanctions evasion. Excludes minor Tier-3/Tier-4 regional banks where systemic blowback is negligible.

cases.name: Chinese Banks threatened under CAATSA/HK Autonomy Act

coverage_note: 7 named major confrontation cycles; captures the universe of high-level sovereign vs major foreign bank showdowns.
known_gaps: Classified or unreported internal Treasury waivers and backroom diplomatic resolutions that never surfaced publicly.
skeleton: Total high-stakes threats against systemically significant global financial institutions versus actual executions resulting in SWIFT/US system cutoffs.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 7 distinct high-stakes confrontation cycles where systemic friction was heavily weighed.
validity_reason: Institutional architecture of US secondary sanctions and the US dollar's dominance remain structurally stable on this horizon.
